Procedural fairness (equal expected proposed prices) enforced exactly; substantive fairness (equal expected accepted prices) measured as cumulative unfairness

settings.definition_quote: Prices are only allowed to be chosen from a known and fixed set of d prices: V = {v_1, ..., v_d}, where 0<v_1<...<v_d<=1. ... we propose a pricing policy pi=(pi^1,pi^2) consisting of two probabilistic distributions ... A customer then arrives with an observable group attribution G_e ... we observe a feedback 1_t^e = 1(v_t^e <= y_t^e) and receive a reward r_t^e = 1_t^e v_t^e.

source.label: theorem:regret_and_unfairness
source.quote: FPA guarantees an $O(\sqrt{T}d^{\frac32}\log{\frac{d\log T}{\epsilon}})$ regret with no procedural unfairness and an $O(\sqrt{T}d^{\frac32}\log{\frac{d\log T}{\epsilon}})$ substantive unfairness with probability $1-\epsilon$.

results.notes: Paper's epsilon is failure probability (mapped to delta); d = number of prices mapped to K. Regret is sum of expected-revenue differences vs. the optimal fair policy (pseudo-regret on per-round policy), holding w.p. 1-eps. Zero procedural unfairness also guaranteed. Constants depend on F_min, q.

source.label: theorem:regret_and_unfairness
source.quote: FPA guarantees an $O(\sqrt{T}d^{\frac32}\log{\frac{d\log T}{\epsilon}})$ regret with no procedural unfairness and an $O(\sqrt{T}d^{\frac32}\log{\frac{d\log T}{\epsilon}})$ substantive unfairness with probability $1-\epsilon$.

results.notes: Cumulative substantive unfairness bound; procedural unfairness is exactly zero.

source.label: theorem:regret_lower_bound
source.quote: Assume $d\leq T^{\frac13}$. Given the online two-group fair pricing problem and the regret definition as \Cref{equ:regret}, any algorithm would at least suffer an $\Omega(\sqrt{dT})$ regret.

results.notes: Proved via reduction to unconstrained pricing (Theorem 17: d fixed prices in [0,c], 3<=d<=T^{1/3}, any algorithm suffers Omega(sqrt(dT))), with a bandit-style construction.

symbols.C_x: regret constant: algorithm has at most C_x*sqrt(T) cumulative regret

conditions: any algorithm with an C_x T^{1/2} cumulative regret and zero procedural unfairness
hard instances: Example 1 (d=3, q=0.3) and its epsilon-perturbation

source.label: theorem:unfairness_lower_bound
source.quote: For any constant $C_x$, there exists constants $C_u>0$ such that any algorithm with an $C_x\cdot T^{\frac12}$ cumulative regret and zero procedural unfairness has to suffer an $C_u\cdot T^{\frac12}$ substantive unfairness.

results.notes: Lower bound on cumulative substantive unfairness restricted to regret-optimal, procedurally fair algorithms; C_u = C_min exp(-exp(2C_x)+3C_x/2)/2.
